jobs.title: Sales Enablement Operations Manager
jobs.location: San Francisco; Remote (United States); Austin; New York City
jobs.description:
Perplexity's sales organization is growing fast, and our sellers need the right content, tools and AI workflows to win. As our first Sales Enablement Operations Manager, you'll be the strategic partner and builder behind how Perplexity's sales team finds, uses and learns from content.

This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with the Sales Enablement Lead to define our content management strategy, including whether to build on Perplexity's own AI platform or buy a dedicated tool. Then you'll build it, run it and keep improving it. You'll also build AI skills, plugins and workflows that make reps and managers faster and more effective every day.

This is a foundational hire. We're looking for someone who can grow into a leadership role as the enablement function scales.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Help shape content and knowledge strategy

 - Partner with the Sales Enablement Lead to define the long-term content management strategy for the sales team, from requirements to the build-vs-buy decision.

 - Work alongside the Sales Enablement Lead on the evaluation: gather stakeholder needs, assess options (including Perplexity Computer and third-party platforms), model costs and tradeoffs, and shape a joint recommendation to sales leadership.

Help build and run the enablement stack

Build AI tools for the sales team

Lead and scale

 - Set the standards for how enablement content and AI tools get built, contributed and maintained across the GTM organization.

 - Act as a trusted thought partner to enablement leadership on priorities, operating model and tooling.

 - Help shape the enablement operations function as the team grows, with a path to leading it.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4–6 years in go-to-market roles, with at least 2 years owning sales enablement operations, revenue operations, GTM systems or sales content strategy.

 - Experience owning a sales content or knowledge system end to end, including taxonomy, governance, adoption and measurement.

 - A track record of leading or heavily shaping a tooling decision, such as a platform evaluation, migration or in-house build.

 - Real, hands-on AI fluency: you've built AI tools or workflows (custom GPTs, Claude or Perplexity skills, MCP connectors, n8n, Zapier, Clay or similar) that other people use regularly, and you can show examples.

 - Systems thinking: you understand how content, CRM, call-recording and communication tools connect, and you design for how sellers actually work.

 - Strong judgment and the ability to make a clear recommendation and defend it with leadership.

 - Experience driving cross-functional projects without formal authority.

 - Clear written and verbal communication, and a bias toward shipping, measuring and iterating.

Nice to have

 - Hands-on experience with enablement platforms such as Highspot, Seismic, Guru, Mindtickle or Showpad.

 - Background as an AE, SE or BDR before moving into enablement or operations.

 - Experience managing or mentoring contractors, interns or direct reports.

 - Experience at a high-growth AI or SaaS company.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - First 6 months: A governed content hub and call library are live and adopted, enablement reporting is in place, and a growing library of AI tools is measurably saving time for reps and managers.

 - First year: Enablement operations is a scalable function with clear standards, and you're ready to lead it as the team grows.

jobs.title: Sales Onboarding Manager
jobs.description:
Perplexity is hiring sellers fast, and every new seller has to learn a fast-moving product line: Enterprise, Comet, Computer and the API. We're looking for a Sales Onboarding Manager to own how new sellers go from their first day to selling on their own. You'll build the program, keep it current, run it, and certify that each seller is ready before they sell independently.

This is a high-ownership, highly visible role on a small Sales Enablement team. You'll partner with the Sales Enablement Lead and work closely with sales leaders, frontline managers, Product, Product Marketing, Solutions and Revenue Operations. Your goal is a robust, relevant, progressive and measurable ramp that gets faster as we scale.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Sales Onboarding Manager owns the onboarding experience for Enterprise and Commercial Account Executives (AEs) and Business Development Representatives (BDRs), from Day 1 through field certification. You'll design the curriculum, keep it up to date as the product changes, lead the sessions yourself, manage the logistics of placing each cohort into the right sessions, and run the certifications that decide when a new hire is ready.

Company-wide new-hire orientation is owned by a separate onboarding role. Ongoing training for ramped sellers is owned by Sales Enablement. You'll partner with both so new sellers move smoothly from orientation into their sales ramp and then into working independently with ongoing training from Enablement.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the sales onboarding program. Co-design and run role-based ramps for BDRs and for Enterprise and Commercial AEs, including learning objectives, milestones and time-to-productivity targets for each stage. Where BDRs and AEs need the same foundations, they learn them together. Where the jobs differ, each gets its own track.

 - Build the BDR ramp. Teach new BDRs prospecting and outbound: ideal customer profile and persona research, account and territory rules, multi-channel sequences, cold calling, cold email, qualification, and clean handoffs to AEs. Get BDRs productive in the prospecting stack, including Salesforce, Apollo and the dialer.

 - Build and maintain content. Create and update modules, playbooks, talk tracks, demo guides, knowledge checks and self-paced content. Update materials as products, pricing, positioning and process change, and retire anything out of date.

 - Facilitate live sessions. Lead engaging, interactive sessions (virtual and in person) on Perplexity's products, sales process, customer personas, discovery, demos, objection handling and tools. Bring in subject-matter experts from Product, Product Marketing, Solutions and top sellers.

 - Run cohort logistics. Work with Recruiting and sales leaders to track incoming hires, assign each one to the right sessions for their role, segment and start date, and manage calendars, attendance, make-ups and pre-work.

 - Certify field readiness. Design and run role-specific certifications using clear rubrics. For BDRs, that means cold-call, email and qualification certifications. For AEs, it means pitch, discovery and demo certifications. Both roles also certify on tools. Calibrate scoring with BDR and sales managers, give actionable feedback, and decide when a new hire is ready to sell on their own.

 - Partner with frontline managers. Give managers visibility into each new hire's progress, flag risks early, and equip managers to reinforce onboarding through coaching and call reviews.

 - Measure and improve. Track completion, certification pass rates and ramp attainment. For BDRs, also track activity, meetings booked and accepted, and pipeline sourced. For AEs, also track time to first meeting, pipeline and closed business. Use the data and new-hire feedback to improve the program each cohort.

 - Scale with leverage. Use AI tools, including Perplexity's own products, to build content faster, personalize learning paths and automate repetitive logistics so the program keeps up with hiring.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The best candidates are strong facilitators who also design programs and run operations well. You can command a room, build a curriculum from a blank page, and keep a complicated cohort calendar running smoothly. You hold a high bar for readiness and know how to tell a manager when a seller isn't there yet.

Must-haves

 - 2–4 years in sales enablement, sales onboarding or sales training, ideally at a high-growth B2B SaaS or AI company. Experience carrying a quota or managing sellers is a strong plus.

 - A track record of designing and running a sales onboarding or ramp program end to end, with measurable impact on ramp time or productivity.

 - Excellent live facilitation, virtual and in person, with sellers at different experience levels, from early-career BDRs to seasoned AEs.

 - Experience designing and running certifications or skills assessments (such as cold-call, pitch, discovery or demo) using rubrics that sales managers trust.

 - Strong program management and operational rigor. You can run several overlapping cohorts, schedules and stakeholders without dropping details.

 - Working knowledge of modern sales methods (such as MEDDICC, Command of the Message or similar), outbound prospecting and the full sales cycle from first touch to close.

 - Comfort learning technical products quickly and explaining them clearly. You can learn an AI product well enough to teach and demo it.

 - Fluency with the sales tech stack, such as Salesforce, a conversation-intelligence tool and an LMS or content-management platform.

 - High ownership and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment where the product changes weekly.

Nice to have

 - Experience onboarding sellers for AI, developer or other technically complex products.

 - Background in instructional design or adult learning.

 - Previous experience as a BDR/SDR or as a BDR/SDR manager.

 - Experience building onboarding for both Enterprise and Commercial/velocity sales motions, or for Customer Success roles.

 - Experience standing up enablement tooling (LMS, content hub, call library) or reporting on ramp metrics.

 - Experience using AI to build content or automate enablement operations

ROLE OVERVIEW

Enterprise admins are among the most important users Harvey serves. At the world's largest law firms and legal departments, IT and security teams are part of every buying decision and every rollout, and they hold Harvey to the most stringent access requirements of any industry, from ethical walls to matter-level permissions. At most companies, admin capabilities are checklist items. At Harvey, they're in the spotlight.

The Senior Product Manager, Admin will own the product vision and roadmap for identity and access on Harvey's admin platform, the operational control surface where enterprise administrators manage users and access, govern permissions, and steer their organization's deployment of Harvey at scale. That spans SSO and login, SCIM and user lifecycle, MFA, permissions and RBAC, external users, and global identity across workspaces. You will also help define a brand-new problem space. As agents become part of how legal work gets done, you'll work with product managers across Harvey to define what agent identity means: how agents authenticate, how admins grant them permissions, and how customers govern them.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone with strong product judgment who can turn complex, high-stakes enterprise problems into a clear strategy and shipped product: running several platform projects at once, moving with urgency, and owning outcomes end to end. You'll partner closely with Engineering, Design, Security, Legal Engineering, and Go-to-Market, and your work will directly shape whether the world's most demanding enterprises trust Harvey with their most sensitive work.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product vision, roadmap, and execution for identity and access at Harvey, taking problems from discovery through launch and iteration.

 - Partner with Engineering, Design, and GTM to deliver scalable, secure, and intuitive admin experiences that meet the operational needs of large enterprise customers.

 - Engage directly with enterprise customers, customer success, and sales teams to deeply understand admin pain points, access and governance requirements, and integration needs, and translate those insights into high-impact product investments.

 - Define agent identity with product managers across Harvey: how agents authenticate, how admins assign them permissions, and how customers govern them.

 - Make feature access provisioning seamless between our go-to-market systems and the product, so customers reach Early Access and GA capabilities without manual work.

 - Build the permission and identity primitives other Harvey teams build on, and partner with Security and Legal Engineering on the controls enterprise buyers require.

 - Establish and track key metrics for provisioning coverage, admin efficiency, and governance, using data to inform prioritization and measure success.

 - Drive alignment across stakeholders on trade-offs, sequencing, and scope, communicating clearly at both the executive and working-team levels.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years of hands-on product management experience building enterprise B2B products, with deep familiarity in identity and access: SSO, SCIM, MFA, RBAC, permissions, and audit logging.

 - A track record of shipping high-quality products end to end in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, running several projects at once, ideally at a startup or growth-stage company that moved upmarket into large enterprises.

 - Platform and systems thinking: you have built something other teams depend on, and you understand how a change in one system ripples through the rest.

 - Experience working directly with security, compliance, and IT stakeholders, such as security reviews or procurement, and shipping products that pass their scrutiny.

 - Strong analytical and communication skills, with experience using data to drive decisions and the ability to articulate a clear product vision to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Enough technical depth to partner with engineers on architecture and tradeoffs, with a strong desire to go deeper.

 - A hungry, curious, ownership-driven approach, with strong attention to detail.




COMPENSATION

$177,700 - $266,500 USD

Harvey is the AI platform trusted by the world's leading law firms and corporate legal teams, and one of the fastest-growing companies in AI. Now we're bringing that to asset management — and this role owns it. We're building the team that will define how the world's leading asset managers, private equity firms, and institutional funds adopt AI. This is a ground-floor opportunity to own a new vertical — we're still proving out this motion, which means the person who joins will help write the playbook.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Develop and manage a named account list across asset management — private equity, venture, private credit, hedge funds, real assets, and institutional allocators (LPs) — and own the full sales cycle from prospecting through contracting and expansion.

 - Build and manage senior relationships across each firm's legal, compliance, and investment teams — typically anchored by a GC, CLO, or CCO — expanding into portfolio-company counsel over time. Understand how decisions get made in these organizations and navigate accordingly.

 - Lead complex, multi-threaded deals with stakeholders ranging from managing directors and general partners to day-to-day legal and compliance users — translating Harvey's AI capabilities into language that resonates with financial buyers.

 - Work closely with product and engineering to stay current on Harvey's capabilities and shape solutions around how asset managers actually work — contract review, due diligence, portfolio company support, regulatory workflows.

 - Conduct tailored demos and presentations that connect Harvey's product directly to the workflows and pain points specific to financial services buyers.

 - Document what works. This team is building the asset management playbook from scratch, and your learnings will directly shape how we scale the motion.



WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience selling complex software or professional services into financial services (ideally asset management, private equity, or institutional funds). You understand how these firms are structured and how buying decisions get made.

 - Proven ability to run a global or named account relationship — you've been the person a firm calls, not just the person who closes a deal and moves on. Ideally you've navigated a fund relationship or portfolio company motion.

 - Background in enterprise software sales, management consulting, or a combination — we're intentionally mixing profiles on this team. If you've unlocked a major financial services account or come from a firm that advises these organizations, we want to talk to you.

 - Comfortable operating in a motion that's still being defined. You're a builder who can prospect independently, iterate on messaging, and contribute to the team's collective learning.

 - Genuine curiosity about AI and how it applies to knowledge-intensive work. You don't need a legal background, but you should be excited about what Harvey is doing and motivated to develop real fluency in the space.

This isn’t a typical SaaS support role: Harvey moves fast, priorities shift often, and you’ll wear multiple hats as the product and team scale. We’re looking for someone who loves problem-solving, thrives with ambiguity, and pairs strong technical instincts with real empathy for enterprise customers.

 - Maintain a high standard of reliability and accountability, ensuring consistent coverage and follow-through during assigned shifts.

 - Collaborate with team members to troubleshoot complex issues, escalating them appropriately when needed.

 - Maintain a deep understanding of our products and services to provide knowledgeable support.

 - Document customer interactions and feedback to aid in continuous improvement of our services.

 - Work closely with other departments to resolve customer issues and contribute to the overall customer experience.

 - Collaborate effectively as part of a team while confidently owning and executing tasks independently.

 - Stay informed of new product features and updates to provide accurate and current support.

 - Contribute to the development and refinement of support processes and materials, such as FAQs and knowledge base articles.



WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 3+ years proven experience in a technical support role, in a fast-paced environment providing “white glove” or “premium support” to large enterprise customers for AI-driven products

 - Exceptional empathy and a genuine desire to help and connect with customers.

 - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to think creatively and resolve complex issues.

 - Excellent organisational skills, capable of managing multiple tasks and priorities effectively.

 - Comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment, with a track record of taking ownership

 - Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to convey complex information in an understandable manner.

 - Understanding of APIs, and ability to explain complex API concepts to both technical and non-technical customers.

 - Familiarity with customer support tools and CRM systems; experience with Zendesk, Salesforce is a plus.

 - Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and build positive working relationships across departments.

 - A passion for learning and personal growth, with a commitment to staying informed about industry trends and best practices.

 - Availability to participate in an on-call rotation outside scheduled working hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, in accordance with the company’s on-call policy.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We're hiring a Sr. Infrastructure Engineer to own the shared layer that every Harvey IT system runs on. You'll join Core IT Engineering & Infrastructure, reporting to Dave Vega, Director of IT, alongside engineers who own identity and collaboration, Microsoft platforms, networking, and client platforms.

Harvey is cloud-first. We run no servers or data centers of our own. Our IT infrastructure is cloud tenants, SaaS configuration, office networks across a growing global footprint, and the automation that ties them together. Today that cross-cutting work is done on the side by each platform owner. This role makes it someone's primary job, so it gets built once, done well, and doesn't break quietly.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

You'll own the shared infrastructure, automation and reliability work that cuts across every IT platform.

 - IT cloud accounts and tenants. Own access, guardrails and cost for the cloud accounts IT runs (AWS, Azure, GCP projects for IT tooling). Be the BizTech engineering partner to Security and Infrastructure on tenant-level changes, such as cloud migrations that touch Entra and M365.

 - Infrastructure as code for IT. Build and run the Git repos, CI pipelines and review process for IT configuration (Okta, Jamf, Intune, Google Workspace). Platform owners keep owning their config. You own the framework they all use.

 - IT automation and provisioning. Own the automation behind identity lifecycle and IT workflows: SCIM and provisioning flows, onboarding and offboarding orchestration across systems, and IT workflows in Serval.

 - Monitoring, backup and resilience. Set up health checks and alerting for critical IT systems and integrations, config drift detection, SaaS backup (Google, Slack, M365) and tested recovery runbooks.

 - Scripts and internal tooling. Take over the scripts and admin utilities that live on individual laptops today. Put them in source control, document them and keep them running.

 - Office site standard. Work with Network and AV/Media teams to define the repeatable technical template for new offices: configuration, monitoring and documentation each site copies. Network and AV build execution stays with their owners.

 - Engineering practices. Raise the bar on change control, documentation and runbooks across the pillar, so primaries and backups can cover for each other.

 - Certificates, domains and DNS. Track and renew every certificate IT depends on (Apple Push, SAML signing, SSL, Wi-Fi/802.1X). Work with Network and CorpSec teams to own and manage DNS NS solutions for IT. Build expiry monitoring to avoid surprises.







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 6+ years in corporate IT engineering, systems engineering or SRE, with at least 2 years owning shared infrastructure or automation for a SaaS-first company.

 - Strong infrastructure-as-code experience. You've managed real systems with Terraform or similar, in Git, with pull-request review and CI.

 - Solid scripting in Python plus one of Bash, PowerShell or Go. You write code other people can read and maintain.

 - Hands-on with identity and provisioning: SAML, OIDC, SCIM and lifecycle automation in Okta or Entra.

 - Working knowledge of at least one major cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP): IAM, accounts and cost basics.

 - Comfort with DNS, TLS and certificate management, and basic enterprise networking.

 - You've built monitoring and alerting that people actually trust, and written runbooks that someone else used successfully.

 - Clear written communication. You can explain a change, its risk and its rollback to non-engineers.


BONUS POINTS

 - Terraform providers for Okta, Google Workspace or Jamf, or config-as-code tools for Intune

 - Serval or similar IT automation platforms

 - SaaS backup and recovery tools for Google Workspace, Slack or M365

 - Multi-site office rollouts across regions, including working with local vendors and ISPs

 - Experience at a fast-growing company where company headcount grew faster than the IT team







COMPENSATION

$153,000 - $210,500 USD

AI is removing much of the repetitive work through which lawyers have always learned and is changing how they work. Firms and legal departments now have to work out how lawyers build judgment, what competence means at each level and how to bring partners along as well as associates. As Transformation Advisory Lead for Talent & Learning, you help them answer those questions. You have built and run lawyer development yourself, so customers trust you to design programs that fit how lawyers actually learn.

You will be one of the first senior specialists in Harvey's Transformation Office. You will help build our talent and learning offering, bring that expertise to client engagements run by our Engagement Managers and join our Practice Directors when a customer has a specific need in talent and learning. What you learn will shape how Harvey advises the market and what we build next.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design how lawyers and legal professionals develop in an AI-native team. Build development models, by seniority and specialism, that replace apprenticeship-era learning with something deliberate that the customer can own.

 - Build learning that changes practice. Design curricula, workshops and programs on how to practice law with AI: fluency, judgment, verification, supervision and client conversations.

 - Engage leaders. Design for how a partnership and GCs make decisions, because team members follow what their leaders role model and reward.

 - Define what good looks like. Help customers set expectations of AI competence at each level and link them to how lawyers are reviewed and promoted.

 - Make it stick. Help customers measure capability before and after, reinforce new habits and renew programs as the technology changes.

 - Build the offering. Create the curricula, frameworks and diagnostics the Transformation Office uses to deliver talent and learning engagements, and turn each engagement into material the wider team can use.

 - Bring your expertise to early conversations. Join Practice Directors and account teams when a customer has a specific need in talent and learning.







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years of experience, including owning learning and development or professional development at a law firm or legal department, or designing and launching a lawyer training program from the ground up. Legal practice experience is a strong plus.

 - Deep craft in adult learning and instructional design for expert professionals, and how to build judgment and skill over time.

 - A deep understanding of how lawyers develop: the apprenticeship model, how judgment forms, what competence looks like at each level and how CLE/CPD and progression frameworks shape training.

 - A track record of changing how skilled, autonomous professionals work, including champions, reinforcement and before-and-after measurement.

 - Credibility with partners, firm and in-house leadership, and the judgment to design for how they each make decisions.

 - Evidence that you have built programs and frameworks that others ran without you.

 - Energy for building something new while the playbook is still being written.

Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Scale our post-training stack, supporting SFT and RL on leading open-weight models.

 - Build distributed rollout infrastructure that coordinates model inference, tool execution, and collection of training experience for long-horizon tasks.

 - Build the infrastructure for reproducible agent environments where models can interact with documents, tools, and external systems during training and evaluation.

 - Own the performance and reliability of training runs, including GPU utilization, checkpointing, failure recovery, and observability.

 - Identify and remove bottlenecks across training and inference to shorten the path from research idea to useful result.

 - Build the internal tools and services the team runs on: training data management and versioning, running evals and browsing results, and launching and tracking training jobs and experiments.

 - Integrate models into production, including serving, latency, cost, and online evaluation, so research reaches customers quickly and safely.

 - Partner closely with researchers to turn experimental workflows into dependable systems while keeping room for rapid experimentation.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience building ML infrastructure, distributed systems, or research tooling, with ownership of performance, reliability, and operation.

 - Strong Python and generalist software engineering skills across backend services, data systems, and internal tools, with familiarity with PyTorch, JAX, or similar ML frameworks.

 - Experience with distributed training or inference, including diagnosing performance bottlenecks and failures across the stack.

 - Understanding of post-training workflows; experience with RL rollouts, agent environments, or sandboxed tool execution is a plus.

 - Practical judgment about what to build versus adopt, and the ability to partner with researchers and ship quickly as needs evolve.

We are hiring for this role across multiple levels.




COMPENSATION

$230,000 - $450,000 USD

ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Member of Technical Staff, Data & Evals in Harvey Research, you’ll build the data and measurement systems that power our post-training, benchmarking, and agent capability efforts.

We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. You’ll own synthetic data pipelines, evaluation design, the tasks and grading behind training environments, and the systems that turn feedback from domain experts into training signals and rewards. These are tasks where correctness often can’t be verified automatically, so defining and measuring quality is a core research challenge. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the work.

We’re looking for research engineers who can build reliable data and evaluation systems, question what a metric actually tells us, and work closely with researchers and legal experts to turn model failures into measurable improvements.

Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build synthetic data pipelines that generate, filter, and curate training and evaluation samples for complex legal reasoning and agentic workflows.

 - Design evaluations and verifiers that reflect real legal work, calibrate them against expert judgment, and investigate where they fail.

 - Build and maintain capability benchmarks like our Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), along with product-focused evals that track how models perform on real customer workflows.

 - Work with legal domain experts to define quality metrics, rubrics, and other grading mechanisms for training and evaluation.

 - Own training and evaluation data quality, including provenance, coverage, and safeguards against contamination.

 - Close the loop from product usage and customer feedback to new evaluations and training data, so models improve where customers need them most.

 - Partner with researchers to investigate model failures, distinguish real gains from misleading metrics, and use findings to guide training and release decisions.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience building data pipelines, ML evaluation systems, or experimentation tooling, with strong Python skills and ownership of production-quality code.

 - A rigorous approach to measurement, including statistical reasoning, experimental design, and understanding when a metric can mislead.

 - The ability to translate ambiguous goals or expert judgment into structured datasets, rubrics, and measurable criteria.

 - Experience with synthetic data, LLM evaluations, automated raters, or preference data is a plus. Strong data and measurement engineering experience close to ML model development is valuable even without prior LLM work.

We are hiring for this role across multiple levels.




COMPENSATION

$230,000 - $450,000 USD

jobs.title: Research Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench.

As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper.

 - Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency.

 - Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail.

 - Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously.

 - Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems.

 - Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

 - A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP.

 - Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show.

 - Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks).

 - High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running.

 - Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research.


EVEN BETTER

 - Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue.

 - Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes.

 - Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization.

 - Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models.

 - Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks.


INTERN QUALIFICATIONS

 - The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program.

 - Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor.

 - The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday.


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 - Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


BE YOU, WITH US

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

jobs.title: Technical Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Technical Product Marketing Manager who can pick up any Baseten product and explain it clearly to the people who buy it. Baseten sells dedicated inference, Model APIs, training and post-training, and the enterprise platform that ties them together. The work behind each one is the same: understand how the product works, know where it stands against the alternatives, and write about it well enough that an ML engineer trusts it and a buyer acts on it.

We’re hiring for this role across multiple product lines. You’ll work on whichever launch, narrative, or competitive gap matters most at the time, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and the rest of product marketing. It’s a good fit for someone who ramps on technical products quickly and wants to be the person who figures out the story.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Positioning & Technical Narrative

 - Own positioning and messaging for Baseten products across inference, Model APIs, training and post-training, and the core platform, written for ML engineers, platform teams, and executive buyers.

 - Work closely with Product and Engineering to understand architecture, tradeoffs, and roadmap, and make sure every technical claim is accurate and backed by how the product actually behaves.

 - Keep product-level messaging consistent with Baseten’s platform narrative so each product story supports the others.

 - Write messaging that is technically credible without getting lost in implementation detail.

Launches & Go-to-Market

 - Build and run launch plans for new products and major capabilities, from internal enablement through external announcement.

 - Decide what deserves a full launch and what should ship through docs, sales enablement, or targeted customer outreach.

 - Create launch assets including messaging briefs, landing pages, technical blog posts, demo storylines, sales decks, one-pagers, and FAQs.

 - Partner with Demand Gen, Sales, Solutions, and Customer Marketing to turn product capabilities into campaigns and deal support.

Competitive & Market Insight

 - Track the competitive landscape across inference providers, model API companies, hyperscalers, and internal DIY platforms, including pricing, packaging, launches, and messaging.

 - Turn that analysis into a clear point of view on where Baseten wins and loses, and use it to sharpen positioning.

 - Talk to customers and sellers to understand buying criteria, objections, and deal blockers, and bring what you learn back to Product and Marketing as concrete recommendations.

Sales Enablement

 - Build battlecards, competitive talk tracks, objection-handling guides, and product training that sellers actually use.

 - Work with Sales and Solutions to find enablement gaps and close them.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in product marketing, technical marketing, or developer marketing, with at least 2 of those years marketing to developers or technical buyers at an infrastructure, developer tools, cloud, data, or AI company.

 - Strong writing. You can take a dense technical topic and make it clear without oversimplifying it, and you have samples to show.

 - Technical fluency. You’re comfortable reading docs, asking engineers specific questions, and getting up to speed on concepts like inference, autoscaling, fine-tuning, and open- vs. closed-weight models.

 - Hands-on competitive analysis experience: you’ve compared products in depth, formed a view, and used it to change positioning, messaging, or how a deal was sold.

 - A track record of learning unfamiliar products and markets quickly and moving between them.

 - Experience launching technical products or capabilities, including deciding what to launch and how.

 - Comfortable owning both strategy and execution: landing pages, decks, one-pagers, and written content, not just frameworks.

 - Experience at a fast-moving startup, working with multiple stakeholders and shifting priorities.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, inference, model serving, or model training and post-training.

 - Experience marketing to ML engineers, platform engineers, infrastructure leaders, or technical executives.

 - Experience building competitive positioning against cloud providers, inference providers, model API companies, or internal platforms.

 - Time in an adjacent role such as solutions engineering, product management, developer relations, technical writing, or industry or equity research covering AI or infrastructure.





BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

jobs.title: Software Engineer II - AI/ML, Neuron Inference, Neuron Inference
jobs.description:
The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon Web Services (AWS) builds the AWS Neuron SDK, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on AWS Trainium machine learning accelerators.
The Neuron Inference organization is at the forefront of optimizing inference performance for a wide range of ML models and model architectures on AWS's custom ML accelerators. We are working across the stack from PyTorch to the hardware-software boundary, our engineers build systematic infrastructure, develop high-performance kernels for ML functions, ensuring every compute unit is fine-tuned for optimal performance for our customers' demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's possible in AI acceleration.
As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers — from frameworks and kernels through to compiler, runtime, and collectives. We not only optimize performance on open weight models but also contribute to future architecture designs and work closely with customers to enable optimal performance on their models. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology.
As a Software Engineer II - AI/ML, you will design and implement business-critical features and own the performance of models on AWS Trainium end to end. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team also collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers.
This role is responsible for development, enablement, and performance tuning of a wide variety of LLM model families, including massive-scale large language models like the GLM, GPT-OSS, Kimi, and beyond. The Model Enablement team works side by side with compiler engineers and runtime engineers to create, build, and tune distributed inference solutions with AWS Trainium.

* https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/neuron/
* https://github.com/aws/aws-neuron-sdk

* https://www.amazon.science/how-silicon-innovation-became-the-secret-sauce-behind-awss-success

Key job responsibilities
This role contributes to building distributed inference support for PyTorch in the Neuron SDK, and tunes models to ensure the highest performance and maximize efficiency running on AWS Trainium. Strong software development in Python, system-level programming, and ML knowledge are all critical to this role. Our engineers collaborate across compiler, runtime, framework, and hardware teams to optimize machine learning workloads for our global customer base. Working at the intersection of software, hardware, and machine learning systems, you'll bring expertise in low-level optimization, system architecture, and ML model acceleration. In this role, you will:
* Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models and frameworks for deployment on custom ML hardware accelerators.
* Participate in all stages of the ML system development lifecycle, including distributed-computing-based architecture design, implementation, performance profiling, hardware-specific optimizations, testing, and production deployment.

* Conduct comprehensive testing, including unit and end-to-end model testing with continuous deployment and releases through pipelines.

You will collaborate with a cross-functional team of applied scientists, systems engineers, and product managers to deliver state-of-the-art inference capabilities for Generative AI applications. Expect regular collaboration with product and engineering partners as you shape solutions that serve customers at scale.

jobs.title: Senior Quantum Applied Research Scientist, Calibration and Decoding
jobs.description:

We're looking for a passionate scientist at the intersection of quantum device physics, quantum calibration, and machine learning.  Hands-on experience developing learned calibration or decoding models and deploying them within real-time quantum control feedback loops, with direct awareness of latency and throughput constraints.

Do you want to help the world build custom AI? We're hiring a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer to drive technical engagement with partners and customers across NVIDIA's open model portfolio, including NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos. The mission is to turn open models into production-ready AI tuned to a specific domain, from post-training through harness optimization. We want any organization to build, own, and run its own AI on open source models, and this role helps the ecosystem get there at scale!
 Unlike most forward deployed roles, our work runs primarily through NVIDIA's partner ecosystem. Our FDEs work side by side with top ecosystem engineering and research teams, co-lead joint customer engagements, and build the recipes and playbooks that help partners succeed and scale. We also work directly with customers when the work calls for it. Are you one of the strongest post-training applied researchers you know? Ready to take a model from a first customer conversation all the way to production? We'd love to meet you.
 What you'll be doing: 
 This role drives AI solutions from discovery and scoping through post-training, harness optimization, and deployment, working alongside partners and customers. Each use case becomes a post-training and harness strategy with the right methods, data, evaluation, and success criteria. Scalable architectures and deployment plans then take the model to production.

It also means making the architecture and hyperparameter choices that improve results. We scale our impact by building reusable recipes, reference pipelines, and playbooks that let partners succeed independently and help the ecosystem mature in building domain-specific AI.

 Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

jobs.title: Senior Context Fusion AI Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
jobs.description:
We are looking for a strong engineer to join the DRIVE Road Structure / Online Mapping / Context Fusion team. In this role, you will help craft and guide the future of our L3/L4 autonomous-driving solution by building a complete, learned 3D/4D world model that fuses navigation, ego-motion, perception, and sensor signals. You will work closely with perception, prediction, planning, and simulation teams to deliver a world representation that is complete, temporally consistent, uncertainty-aware, and robust enough to drive through the most challenging roads and intersections in L3/L4 autonomy level. 
 This role is central to our vision for AV: developing a shared multimodal scene representation that can jointly support road understanding, 3D object and occupancy perception, motion prediction, and route-conditioned planning. Are you interested in inventing human-level AI for navigation in the unconstrained world under any conditions? If so, join us ! 
 What You'll Be Doing: 
 Design and develop learning-based, multimodal sensor-fusion systems that transform synchronized sensor history, ego-motion, navigation context, and driving context into a unified spatiotemporal world representation. 
 Build architectures that jointly reason over camera, LiDAR, radar, and vehicle-state inputs, with appropriate handling of calibration, synchronization, coordinate transforms, sensor latency, and uncertainty. 
 Develop end-to-end and multi-task models that produce driving-relevant outputs from a shared scene representation, including; road graph elements such as lanes, boundaries, crosswalks, and traffic controls; semantic scene understanding; occupancy and free-space representations, including uncertain and occluded regions; 
 Develop scalable multimodal fusion architectures, including Transformer-based early, late, and hierarchical fusion; BEV, point/voxel, and image-based representations; temporal context aggregation; and cross-modal attention. 
 Create training, fine-tuning, and evaluation pipelines for large-scale multimodal datasets. Define multi-task objectives and metrics that balance perception quality, geometric consistency, prediction accuracy, latency, and safety-critical behavior. 
 Investigate foundation-model approaches for autonomous driving, including vision-language models, multimodal pre-training, representation learning, and efficient deployment of learned world models. 
 Work closely with perception, mapping, prediction, planning, simulation, data, and embedded-software teams to convert research advances into robust, production-quality AV systems. 
 Develop systematic analysis and debugging tools for model failures, cross-sensor disagreement, long-tail scenarios, distribution shift, and regressions in closed-loop simulation and on-road evaluation. 
 What We Need To See: 
 BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience. 
 8+ years of experience, with at least 2+ years in the AV or robotics industry and 2+ years of leadership experience in a technically area
 Strong experience developing production-quality sensor-fusion, perception, state-estimation, or autonomous-driving systems. 
 Demonstrated experience with learning-based multimodal perception or fusion involving two or more cameras, LiDAR, radar, map, navigation, and ego-motion signals. 
 Solid understanding of 3D geometry, coordinate frames, calibration, temporal synchronization, ego-motion compensation, tracking, uncertainty estimation, and sensor failure modes. 
 Experience with deep-learning methods for 3D perception, lego-context scene representation, occupancy/occlusion prediction, semantic segmentation, object detection/tracking, motion prediction, or planning. 
 Strong C++ and Python programming skills, with hands-on experience developing, training, and optimizing deep-learning models in PyTorch. Experience with CUDA, distributed training, mixed-precision techniques, and efficient GPU inference using NVIDIA software and hardware is highly valued. 
 Experience with Transformer, VLM, or multimodal foundation-model architectures, including pre-training, fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, or efficient inference. 
 Experience training and evaluating models at scale, including distributed training, dataset curation, offline evaluation, simulation-based validation, and production monitoring. 
 Ability to work across research and engineering boundaries: turn an ambiguous AV problem into measurable technical objectives, build the solution, and drive it to deployment.

Do you want to be part of a team that's revolutionizing the field of AI with data center scale solutions? We are looking for a hardworking Solution Architect with experience in designing, building, and maintaining large-scale HPC and AI infrastructure to join our team at NVIDIA.
 As Solution Architects, we are actively helping make AI Factories a reality. Working closely with customers and partners to address unsolved problems in the industry, our team helps to deploy and operationalize AI solutions at scale.
 What you'll be doing: 
 Our day-to-day work involves helping our partners be successful in their adoption of end-to-end AI solutions using NVIDIA's compute, networking, and software stacks. For this particular role, that means having a deep technical understanding of NVIDIA Reference Architectures, and using that understanding to enable customers adopting our CPU-based solutions as part of the overall NVIDIA AI Factory. This is a multi-faceted role necessitating being comfortable working on not just hardware and software elements, but also the larger AI workflow and operationalization of large scale compute resources. We succeed when we help our customers overcome barriers to adopting our best known methods. As the technical leader for the CPU components within the NVIDIA AI Factory, you will play an instrumental role in driving that success.
 If this sounds exciting to you, then NVIDIA might be your new home. As a team, we also excel at sharing knowledge with our colleagues, whether it's delivering demos, assisting with proof-of-concepts, or writing papers and developer blogs. By collaborating with executives and engineering, we tackle sophisticated problems and help bring NVIDIA's premiere technologies to life. Our mission is to solve the problems that nobody else has solved yet, and we need someone to be an instrumental part of that!
 What we need to see: 
 Experience with defining, deploying, and testing large scale reference architectures for High Performance Computing and AI.
 A track record of defining and using MLOps and AI workflow tools and processes.

jobs.description:
NVIDIA is looking for a Day 2 Site Reliability Engineer to join the EMEA NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP) Day 1 / Day 2 Operations team. EMEA NCP fleets are scaling towards a million deployed GPUs, and this role exists to keep those fleets running at maximum goodput once they are in production — owning fault detection and remediation, preventive maintenance, and proactive firmware and field-notice rollout across partner estates.
 We are looking for a hands-on reliability engineer who thinks in SLOs, error budgets and blast radius rather than tickets. You will measure and drive MTBI and job goodput on multi-thousand-GPU clusters, automate the detection-to-remediation loop, and work directly with NCP operations teams, NVEX and TAMs to review incidents and escalations and turn each one into a permanent fix.
 NCP estates are open-source-first, home-grown and heterogeneous — upstream Kubernetes, KubeVirt, Slurm, Prometheus/Grafana, Cumulus/SONiC and a long tail of ISV and in-house tooling — so this role is deliberately tool-agnostic: you will meet each partner on the stack they actually run rather than on a single proprietary product, and you will keep GPU capacity generating revenue instead of burning cost in reactive support.
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Own Day 2 production stability and reliability at fleet scale across EMEA NCP partners: define, measure and improve MTBI and job goodput on multi-thousand-GPU clusters, and hold the error budget for the platforms you support.
 Build and operate the fault detection to remediation loop—GPU, node, fabric and storage fault signatures, automated triage, node drain, cordon, reset and return-to-service workflows—so failures are caught and cleared before they cost training jobs.
 Run preventive maintenance and proactive firmware and field-notice rollout campaigns across partner fleets (e.g. CPLD and switch firmware levels), including risk assessment, staged rollout, maintenance-window planning and verification at scale.
 Own observability and reliability tooling for GPU fleets: Prometheus/Grafana/Loki, DCGM and XID diagnostics, node-level health agents such as GPUd and NVSentinel, and fleet-wide reliability intelligence—extending or integrating them into the partner’s own home-grown stack.
 Lead incident response and post-incident review in collaboration with NVEX, TAM and partner operations teams: drive root-cause analysis on escalations, track corrective actions to closure, and convert every recurring incident into automation, a health check or a runbook.
 Own Kubernetes node lifecycle and reliability engineering on heterogeneous open stacks—upstream Kubernetes, KubeVirt, Slurm and GPU-aware schedulers—covering node health policy, upgrade and reboot orchestration, and safe workload draining on GPU-accelerated nodes.
 What We Need to See: 
 BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or related fields, or equivalent experience.
 8+ years in SRE, production engineering or large-scale infrastructure operations roles.
 Reliability Engineering Practice: Demonstrated ownership of production reliability at scale—SLO and error-budget definition, on-call and incident command, blameless post-incident review, and measurable improvement of availability or mean time between interruptions.
 GPU & HPC Fleet Operations: Hands-on experience operating HPC/AI clusters and NVIDIA GPU-accelerated infrastructure—driver and CUDA toolkit lifecycle, firmware management, workload profiling, and troubleshooting across CPUs, GPUs and high-speed interconnects.
 Kubernetes at Scale: Extensive expertise in running Kubernetes in GPU-accelerated and HPC environments—node lifecycle, upgrades and draining, scheduler behaviour, batch schedulers such as Slurm, and mixed bare-metal/virtualised (e.g. KubeVirt) multi-tenant estates.
 Observability & Automation: Proficiency in Python and Bash, Infrastructure-as-Code and configuration management (e.g. Ansible, Terraform), GitOps-based fleet lifecycle and upgrade management, and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki) for monitoring, alerting and building fault-tolerant systems.
 Linux, Storage & Networking Fundamentals: Deep knowledge of Linux (RedHat, Ubuntu), OS-level tuning and security, data centre networking fundamentals, and parallel/enterprise storage (Lustre, GPFS, ZFS, XFS) as they affect cluster stability.
 Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: 
 Experience defining and running proactive firmware, microcode or field-notice rollout campaigns across a large production fleet.
 Familiarity with GPU health and fleet telemetry tooling—DCGM and XID diagnostics, GPUd, NVSentinel, node-level health agents and fleet-wide reliability intelligence.
 Experience with the NVIDIA GPU and Network Operators for automated GPU and network resource lifecycle management in Kubernetes, and with NVIDIA Base Command Manager (BCM) for provisioning and monitoring GPU clusters at scale.
 Practical background in AI-native scheduling and inference frameworks on Kubernetes (e.g. KAI, Grove, Dynamo, NVIDIA Cloud Functions) and their failure modes under load.
 Expertise in RDMA-based fabrics (InfiniBand or RoCE) in HPC or AI environments. Exposure to Cumulus Linux, SONiC or Spectrum-X fabrics, DPU/DOCA infrastructure services, and NVLink/NVSwitch partition operations (NMX-C / NMX-M) on NVL72-class systems is a strong plus.

jobs.title: Lakebase Sales Specialist, Benelux
jobs.description:
SLSQ327R350
 Databricks is seeking a Lakebase Sales Specialist to help customers modernise their operational data foundation with Databricks Lakebase , our fully-managed Postgres offering for intelligent applications . This high-impact role sits within the Lakebase Go-To-Market team and partners closely with regional Account Executives to drive adoption of Lakebase with platform, application, and data teams.
 Lakebase gives customers a unified, governed foundation for operational workloads and AI-native applications , helping them move away from a fragmented estate of point databases toward a modern, scalable, serverless Postgres service. If you want to be at the forefront of operational databases for AI and intelligent applications at one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world, this is your opportunity.
 The impact you will have:  
 Drive new Lakebase revenue by identifying, qualifying, and driving Lakebase activations and consumption within a defined territory, in partnership with regional Account Executives and the broader account team
 Lead with outcomes for key Lakebase personas, including platform teams and developers , data teams , and central IT, articulating how Lakebase helps them ship features faster, simplify operational data architectures, and improve governance and cost efficiency
 Sell the value of fully-managed Postgres for intelligent applications , positioning Lakebase as the optimal choice for operational workloads that power real-time, AI-driven experiences
 Run complex sales cycles from discovery and value hypothesis through commercial negotiation and close, navigating executive, technical, and line-of-business stakeholders
 Orchestrate proof-of-value and POCs that validate Lakebase’s benefits for OLTP-style workloads, reverse ETL, and AI/ML-driven applications, in partnership with solution architects and specialists
 Compete and win against legacy and cloud-native operational databases by leveraging our compete assets, benchmarks, and customer references
 Align to measurable business outcomes such as performance, developer productivity, time-to-market for new features, cost reduction, and simplification of the operational data landscape
 Partner cross-functionally with Product Management, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partner teams to shape territory plans, launch plays, and co-selling motions with key ISVs and GSIs
 Enable the field by sharing Lakebase best practices, success stories, and sales motions with broader sales teams, helping scale Lakebase proficiency across the organisation
 What success looks like in this role: 
 This role requires the ability to operate across two key motions simultaneously:
 Establish top strategic focus accounts by engaging application development teams to create net-new intelligent applications leveraging Lakebase
 Drive longer-term Postgres standardisation and migration within Databricks' most strategic accounts
 Success in this role requires strength in four areas:
 Business ownership: Operate at a business-unit level by tracking revenue, pipeline, and key observations, and by identifying areas needing additional focus or support.
 Strategic account engagement: Partner with account teams to engage priority accounts, driving strategic opportunities from initial engagement through successful outcomes.
 Field, account, & customer enablement: Align customers and the field on the value of Lakebase by equipping AEs and SAs with the messaging and execution motions needed to confidently own accounts without specialist intervention.
 Market voice and thought leadership: Develop an internal and external presence, and by representing Databricks at key first- and third-party events.
 The interview process is designed to evaluate candidates across all four of these dimensions.
 What we look for: 
 Relevant enterprise sales experience , consistently exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder deals
 Proven success selling data platforms, operational databases (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, cloud-native DBaaS), or adjacent data/AI infrastructure to technical buyers and business leaders
 Strong understanding of modern data and application architectures , including cloud-native services, microservices, event-driven systems, and how operational data underpins AI and analytics strategies
 Ability to sell to both technical stakeholders (developers, architects, data engineers) and business stakeholders (product leaders, operations, line-of-business owners)
 Demonstrated experience leading specialist or overlay motions , working jointly with core Account Executives to create and progress opportunities
 Executive presence with the ability to whiteboard architectures , lead C-level conversations, and build trust with senior decision makers
 Strong value selling skills: adept at discovering pain, building a business case, and tying technical capabilities to clear, quantified outcomes
 Excellent communication, storytelling, and negotiation skills, with comfort presenting to both large and small audiences
 Bachelor’s degree
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience selling Postgres, operational databases, OLTP workloads, or transactional cloud database services , ideally within large or strategic accounts
 Familiarity with data platforms, lakehouse architectures, and cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP), including how operational databases fit within broader data and AI strategies
 Understanding of reverse ETL, real-time decisioning, and operational analytics use cases, and how they drive value for customer-facing and internal applications
 Exposure to AI-native and agent-driven applications that depend on low-latency, highly scalable operational data services
 Prior experience in a high-growth, category-creating environment , helping shape new plays, messaging, and customer narratives
 Experience collaborating with partners and ISVs to drive joint pipeline and co-sell motions

jobs.title: Sr. Collections Analyst
jobs.description:
GAQ128R85
 Databricks is looking for a Senior Collections Analyst to own a high-volume accounts receivable (AR) portfolio in a fast-growing, usage-based SaaS business. The role drives timely collections, reduces delinquency, protects cash flow and leads recovery on complex, high-value accounts, while helping shape credit risk decisions. Working closely with Sales, Legal, Billing, Revenue Operations, Cash Application and Finance leadership to resolve disputes, billing gaps and customer escalations, the role has a measurable impact on DSO and bad debt exposure and requires regular overlap with EMEA and PST business hours.
 Job Description
 Own end-to-end portfolio collections and recovery strategies, partnering cross-functionally to resolve high-value escalations, influence credit risk decisions, and drive measurable performance across DSO, aging buckets, and bad debt exposure.
 Design and run recovery strategies for accounts that are structurally delinquent or high-risk.
 Lead cross-functional escalation forums for disputed high-value accounts.
 Present portfolio-level risk trends and actionable insights to Finance leadership.
 Recommend credit limit changes, payment term changes or account holds based on behavioral analytics.
 Work with Legal on pre-legal actions and structured recovery plans.
 Assess creditworthiness, establish risk controls, and lead complex recoveries to protect working capital and minimize bad debt exposure.
 Build scalable reporting models that give clear visibility into aging, dispute velocity and payment predictability.
 Flag worsening payment patterns, and provide quarterly bad debt reserve inputs with documented risk rationale for each account.
 Act as the subject matter expert on usage-based billing disputes and contract interpretation. Resolve complex disputes about usage, contract terms and invoicing discrepancies.
 Handle exceptions from automated dunning, and lead the clean-up of aged AR.
 Manage high-volume customer communication and escalations in Collections Tool, with structured follow-through.
 Work with Cash Application to keep unapplied cash low and resolve posting gaps.
 Find the systemic billing, consumption or process gaps that cause repeat delinquency. Work with Billing and Revenue Operations to put corrective frameworks in place.
 Perform detailed account reconciliations in NetSuite to keep AR accurate and audit-ready.
 Help standardize collections processes so they are faster and can scale, and support user acceptance testing (UAT) for new or improved systems.
 Requirements
 Bachelor's degree in Finance or Accounting is a must. Additional Accounting Qualification is a plus.
 10+ years of collections experience, ideally with both public/private technology companies.
 A track record of owning large, complex, high-value AR portfolios with measurable impact on DSO and cash.
 Working knowledge of usage-based billing models and contract structures.
 Demonstrated ownership of high-value, complex AR portfolios with material cash impact.
 A proven ability to influence commercial stakeholders in high-pressure recovery situations.
 Experience supporting reserve discussions and credit risk decisions.
 Strong commercial judgment, balancing revenue protection against the risk to customer relationships.
 Ability to synthesize large data sets into executive-level risk insights.
 Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
 Hands-on experience with NetSuite / Salesforce with fluency with AI tools, including automated dunning solutions is preferred.

GAQ427R247
 Primary location(s) preferred, but candidates based in SF, Mountain View, NYC, Boston, Chicago, or Denver will also be considered.
 What we look for: 
 The Senior Counsel, Employment will provide sophisticated, practical legal advice to the Databricks People Team and business leaders, with a particular focus on HR AI adoption, compensation and benefits, pay equity, global mobility, employee privacy, and M&A (diligence, employee-related deal terms, and workforce integration). This person will be based in the U.S. and advise directly on U.S. matters, but will also lead and project-manage complex global projects. Regular cross-functional partners will include recruiting, privacy and product legal, security, tax, people operations, comp and benefits, and corporate development.
 The successful candidate will be a pragmatic and resourceful advisor and an enthusiastic AI user, with strong project-management discipline and the ability to move quickly while maintaining a high standard of legal and operational precision. In addition to the focus areas above, this person will collaborate to resolve U.S. disputes.
 This is a full-time position reporting to Databricks' Senior Director and Associate General Counsel of Global Employment Legal and working closely with a team of employment lawyers and legal professionals across multiple regions.
 Responsibilities 
 Advise on cash compensation programs, bonus and incentive plans, clawback policies, equal-pay requirements, pay equity reviews, compensation governance, and related internal and external disclosures. Lead or support pay equity projects, including scoping, data and process review, coordination with stakeholders, review of analyses, and development of remediation or communication plans.
 Provide legal advice on employee benefits, including retirement plans, welfare and wrap plans, severance plans, leave-related benefits, and country-specific benefits and protections, partnering with benefits counsel and regional employment legal team members as appropriate.
 Draft, review, and update employment-related plans, policies, agreements, templates, and employee communications with exceptional precision and attention to detail.
 Advise recruiting and talent acquisition teams on candidate-facing issues, offer letters, employment agreements, compensation terms, background checks, hiring practices, and negotiations, often on time-sensitive matters.
 Advise on global mobility and immigration matters, including employee transfers, international assignments, work authorization, permanent residence processes, employer-of-record and professional-employer-organization arrangements, cross-border moves, and related onboarding or exit issues.
